title: Seal delimiter guard and toolcall watermarking to stabilize SSE partial-JSON reassembly
author: Maya Singh
description: Motivation: customers (via SUP-4421) reported intermittent failures when consuming SSE streams through the OpenAI-compat adapter: partial JSON fragments would sometimes be emitted with duplicated delimiters or with tool/function call sentinel tokens split across chunk boundaries. This resulted in downstream JSON parsers seeing spurious extra delimiters or mis-ordered tool call events. The issue is exacerbated when clients re-chunk the stream (proxies/load balancers) or when multi-byte UTF-8 sequences split across frames. This PR introduces two complementary defenses: (1) a "seal" delimiter guard that normalizes and pins boundary tokens to prevent delimiter coalescing and accidental duplication during reassembly, and (2) a lightweight watermarking token inserted for function/tool call handoff that preserves ordering and enables safe dedup/replay recovery. Changes are implemented in the SSE parser/adapter layer so they are backward-compatible with existing OpenAI-compat clients but harden against the classes of partial-json/delimiter bugs we've seen in production. Summary of changes: added an event-sealing stage in the stream pipeline that rewrites ambiguous delimiter runs into canonical sealed forms; added a seq-watermark header for toolcall events so downstream adapters can detect out-of-order or duplicate handoffs; extended the reassembly window and introduced a small rollback heuristic keyed by watermark+seqid to replay previously emitted partial frames when a late-arriving continuation corrects a boundary. Compatibility notes: clients that parse raw bytes will not observe the watermark tokens unless they opt into an opt-in header (X-RIW-Watermark: enable) exposed on the OpenAI-compat endpoints; by default the watermark is present but encoded as an ignorable sentinel ( series) to avoid breaking strict JSON consumers. Tests: new deterministic unit tests covering UTF-8 split points, fuzz tests for random chunk sizes, integration tests exercising an nginx-based re-chunker in front of the adapter, and a small end-to-end canary that validates behavior against the hosted API. Rollout plan: feature gated by runtime flag sse.seal_delimiter_guard (off by default), will be enabled in canary pool for 48h with traffic mirroring to `slo-canary` dashboards; on success enable in main. See linked Linear tasks for release notes and customer-schedule coordination.
commits_summary: 6 commits: initial parser refactor to introduce 'seal' stage; sanitizer for delimiter runs; watermark token generator and seq id plumbing; reassembly rollback heuristic; extended unit + fuzz tests; docs and changelog entries.
review_comments: Owen Park: Nice approach. Can you explain why we chose "sealed" canonical forms instead of stricter framing that injects an explicit length-prefix? Concern is we add more subtle transformation logic.

Maya Singh: We considered length-prefixing but it breaks compatibility with many proxies and the OpenAI-compat wire expectations. Sealing is a minimal transform that normalizes ambiguous delimiter runs and is reversible for diagnostics. Added tests showing proxies that re-chunk still converge to canonical form.
Isabel Turner: Please validate memory usage for the extended reassembly window under high concurrent connections. We need to ensure no OOM risk.
Maya Singh: Added a bounded window (max 8KB per connection) and a GC path that wakes on pressure; included microbenchmarks in the PR. See metrics in CI artifacts.
Diego Alvarez: Could the watermark sentinel collide with user-provided unicode? What's the plan for clients that will see the sentinel?

Maya Singh: We use Private Use Area (U+E000..U+F8FF) and also provide opt-out via header. The default encoding wraps watermark as an ignorable sentinel -prefixed token that OpenAI-compat SDKs strip automatically. Documented in docs/compatibility.
Owen Park: CI flaked once on the fuzz harness; reran and all green. Approving now.
Isabel Turner: Approved after memory safeguards and test additions.
ci_checks: bench: pass (seal stage adds 1.8% p99 tail cost for tiny streams)
release_notes: Fixes multiple classes of SSE partial-JSON boundary bugs: normalizes delimiter runs to avoid duplication, preserves function/tool-call ordering via watermarking, provides rollback heuristic to resolve late-arriving continuation frames. Backwards-compatible; opt-out header available for early integrators.
rollout_plan: Enable feature flag in canary pool for 48h, mirror 10% of traffic, watch slo-canary dashboard for boundary-misalignment and json-parse-error metrics. If stable, flip flag globally; provide opt-out header for customers requiring raw byte fidelity.
notes_for_ops: If customers report increased p99 token latency for tiny streams, disable sse.seal_delimiter_guard and collect sample traces. The GC threshold and reassembly window are adjustable via runtime flags (see runtime/config/feature_flags.rs).
